subject.title: agentmemory__memory_search returns "index metadata is missing" persistently (memory-core manager state cache)

question: Should this issue remain the umbrella for builtin, QMD, and external AgentMemory failures, or should OpenClaw retain only a narrowed core reproduction and route the external tool separately?
rationale: Current main shows distinct manager implementations and no source-backed evidence that every reported backend emits the same failure from the same cause; choosing a single repair boundary without that decision risks a misleading core fix.

options.title: Narrow to a core reproduction
options.body: Keep a single OpenClaw issue only after a current builtin or QMD gateway reproduction identifies the exact manager and captures CLI-versus-tool state.

options.title: Split by owner
options.body: Create or link separate owner reports for builtin memory-core, QMD, and the installed AgentMemory integration so each fix has one runtime contract.

options.title: Document restart-only semantics
options.body: Treat persisted memory configuration changes as requiring an explicit gateway reload and focus follow-up solely on error wording and recovery guidance.

recommendation.title: Narrow to a core reproduction
recommendation.body: Keep a single OpenClaw issue only after a current builtin or QMD gateway reproduction identifies the exact manager and captures CLI-versus-tool state.

likelyOwner.reason: Their related proposal and real gateway proof give the strongest available routing context for the original builtin stale-manager portion, while the broader backend split still needs owner confirmation.
